author: Fritz. Ludwig
title: A Sinking Ship.
content:
Let’s all be honest here, my fellow Roblox players: this site/app is a sinking ship. When you look at how 1984-adjacent Roblox has become, you’ll understand what I mean. 

First, the chat update. Yes, it’s the update that started the downward spiral that Roblox is currently stuck in. Before the chat update, anyone could talk to anyone, though parents of child players could restrict chat access. There was certainly a pr*d problem, but rather than hiring more moderators and actually putting in work to fix things… they instead chose the route of age segregation. 

Now, you HAVE to scan your face so you can use the chat, but since the scan uses AI to determine your age, there’s a non-zero chance you’ll be put in the wrong age bracket. How does Roblox fix this problem? By requiring a user to submit their driver’s license, of course! Do you see the issue? This is NOT a good idea, especially not for solving the pr*d problem. Now, the age brackets are as follows; 
>9 (May chat with users aged under 13.)
9-12 (May chat with users aged under 16.)
13-15 (May chat with users aged 9-17)
16-17 (May chat with users 13-20)
18-20 (May chat with users aged 16 and older)
21+ (May chat with users 18 and older)

There are a few glaring problems with this; for one, a pr*d could use the face of a younger relative to be put into a certain age bracket so they can gr**m or ab*se children in the age group they’re into. For another, here’s the age percentages of the player base; 22% is under 9, 23% are 9-12, 15% are 13-16, 21% are 17-24, 17% are 25 or older, and 1% have an unknown age.
So, older players get to chat with less and less players, while pr*ds can put themselves into any age group they’d want with enough gumption. What a joy! 

That’s just the first part of the whole problem. Next, the avatar customization changes. 

Now, before 2026, there was a FLOURISHING market involving the classic faces. Some people staked over thousands of dollars in the classic faces, but what do you know, Roblox decided to go and ruin that, too. And you want to know what they replaced it with? 
3D faces made to specifically track the facial expressions of players and mirror it onto their avatar’s face. Is that not concerning to anyone else?

They also appear to be gearing up to remove R6, a very common rig system that MANY people (including myself) use for their avatars. Yes, Baszucki promised that R6 would be kept safe, but he promised the same thing about classic faces. 

All in all? Roblox is a sinking ship riddled with problems. TLDR; It’s not far off to compare modern Roblox to 1984.

author: GenuinePeaknessAJ
title: It’s good! Just not very safe
content: At its core, Roblox isn't just a single video game; it is an expansive engine for user-generated content. It provides a virtual space where players can build, share, and experience millions of games together. From complex role-playing worlds to obstacle courses ("obbies") and tycoon simulators, there is something for every interest. Through Roblox Studio, the platform introduces millions of young people to programming, 3D design, and digital entrepreneurship. It serves as a digital hangout space where kids can stay connected with real-world school friends, especially through private servers. Despite its cartoonish, child-friendly aesthetic, Roblox’s open-communication framework presents significant safety vulnerabilities. Because millions of children share the space with adults, bad actors frequently use anonymous accounts to target minors. Law enforcement agencies have repeatedly warned that predators pose as peers, use the in-game currency (Robux) to manipulate victims, and attempt to move kids off the platform to unmonitored messaging apps like Discord or Snapchat. While Roblox has implemented filters, critics and legal investigations highlight that adult users can easily bypass default restrictions by lying about their age during sign-up. The volume of user-generated content makes total moderation difficult. Hidden "underground" games with sexually explicit themes or mature voice chats occasionally bypass the automated filters before being reported and taken down. Is Roblox worth playing? Yes, but never unmonitored. The platform features extensive, built-in safety mechanics, but they must be manually managed by an adult, if your child does play them I recommend Creating a parent account, link it to your child’s profile, and lock down the communication settings so only approved "Friends" can message them. For younger children, completely disable private messaging and public chat features. Encourage your kids to play on private servers with real-life friends rather than opening their sessions to the public. Teach your child to never share personal information, accept gifts from strangers, or agree to migrate a conversation to another app.Overall, it’s worth a try, just not very safe.
